subject: Atelier + Redwood: on-prem LLM access — link-layer choice (VPC peering / PrivateLink / S2S VPN)
messages:
From: Lucas Moreau <lucas@atelier-analytics.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 30 Jul 2025 09:12:00 +0200
Subject: Atelier + Redwood: on-prem LLM access — link options

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for taking this — quick context from our side: Atelier is evaluating Redwood Private for an on-prem inference deployment where data never leaves our VPC. Our infra team asked for a recommendation between VPC peering, PrivateLink (AWS endpoint service), or site-to-site VPN for production traffic. High-level constraints:

- Latency SLO: 50ms p95 from our application fleet to inference nodes.
- Security: Security/compliance team requires no traffic through the public internet; prefer private endpoints and least-privilege routing.
- IP model: We need to avoid large IP remaps; keep routing simple for network ops.
- Scale: Expected sustained ~100 req/s with bursts to 400 req/s during peaks.
- Timeline: PoC in 2 weeks, production target in 8–10 weeks.

Can you share guidance on tradeoffs and an opinionated recommendation (what we should do for PoC vs production)? Also, example timeline and checklist for each path (certs, NAT, route tables, firewall rules, acceptance steps).

If it helps, attaching our current network CIDR list and initial security constraints (will send separately).

Appreciate it —
Lucas Moreau
CTO, Atelier Analytics
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
To: Lucas Moreau <lucas@atelier-analytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jul 2025 18:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Atelier + Redwood: on-prem LLM access — link options

Hi Lucas — thanks for the clear constraints. TL;DR recommendation below, followed by a short tradeoff table and proposed next steps.

TL;DR:
- PoC (2 weeks): site-to-site VPN for fastest unblock (low setup friction).
- Production (recommended): AWS PrivateLink (endpoint service) as primary for security/isolation, with VPC peering as a conditional fallback only if low-latency strictness can't be met via PrivateLink and both VPCs are co-located and managed. Avoid S2S VPN for prod due to jitter, scale limits, and operational overhead.

Why: short tradeoff summary
- Latency:
  - VPC peering: best path (L3 routing) — lowest added RTT. Good when both sides are in same cloud region/account or have cross-account peering agreement.
  - PrivateLink: adds an extra hop (ENI + NLBs) but typically satisfies sub-50ms in-region. Better isolation (no route table exposure).
  - S2S VPN: variable latency/jitter; fine for PoC but risky for tight SLOs at scale.

- Security & blast radius: PrivateLink > VPC peering > VPN. PrivateLink only exposes the service interface and is easiest to audit. Peering exposes entire IP ranges (need careful route/ACLs).

- Operational complexity & troubleshootability:
  - PrivateLink: operationally simple once accepted; you manage endpoint acceptance, SGs, and IAM. Good observability (endpoint metrics + Redwood side logs).
  - Peering: simple routing but requires careful IP plan and mutual route management across teams.
  - VPN: quick to stand up, but requires continuous monitoring (BGP, tunnels) and can be flaky during maintenance.

- Scalability & cost:
  - PrivateLink: predictable per-GB pricing and scales behind AWS NLBs; may incur cross-AZ charges.
  - Peering: cheap (no per-GB charges in same region) but can be harder to partition per-tenant.
  - VPN: cheap-ish but not designed for sustained high throughput at low latency.

Recommended path & fallback logic:
1) Start PoC with S2S VPN to validate application-level integration and run perf tests (2 weeks).
2) Simultaneously provision PrivateLink on our side (we'll create an endpoint service) and share the acceptance steps with Atelier.
3) After PoC perf data: if PrivateLink p95 latency meets your 50ms SLO, go direct to PrivateLink for production. If not, evaluate peering for the production lane (requires IP renumbering or careful route filters).

Checklist for each option (high-level):
- Common: mutual TLS for app-level auth, IP allowlist, and service account with least-privilege.
- PrivateLink: create endpoint service on Redwood, provide service name, you create interface endpoint in your VPC, share SGs and acceptance steps, exchange required principal ARNs. Confirm cross-account endpoint acceptance process and provide test harness (we can supply a small test token).
- Peering: confirm non-overlapping CIDRs, create peering connection, add routes, adjust security groups, test traceroute and perf.
- S2S VPN: exchange tunnel endpoints, pre-shared keys or certificate-based auth, BGP pref if needed, route filters, NF/IPS rules.

Attachments: I attached a short connectivity matrix (redwood-onprem-connectivity-matrix.pdf) and a proposed MOP for Atelier (proposal-atelier-mop.docx) with the step-by-step acceptance plan.

Next steps I propose (actionable):
1) You confirm PoC acceptance of an S2S VPN for initial testing — confirm subnets/CIDRs and who on your netops will accept endpoint creation (name + email).
2) We'll create a PrivateLink endpoint service and share the service name + IAM role needed for acceptance (ETA: 3 business days).
3) Run a short perf test (we'll provide a lightweight test client) and decide on peering only if PrivateLink fails latency tests.

Questions for you: can you share the exact CIDR blocks for the app fleet and the security contact who will accept endpoint connections? Also confirm whether certificate-based VPN auth is required (we can do PSK for PoC, certs for prod).

Thanks —
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

+1 on the PrivateLink-first approach for prod. One operational note: if Atelier's security policy forbids any route exchange, PrivateLink is the only clean option.

Operational asks from our side (so we can prepare infra):
- Confirm whether you want endpoint ownership to be on Atelier or Redwood (this affects who accepts the service).
- If Atelier wants us to own the endpoint service, we will need the principal ARN(s) for the account(s) that will create the interface endpoints.
- Confirm expected throughput per AZ (helps size NLBs and plan for cross-AZ charges).

We'll standby to open the endpoint service and prepare the acceptance workflow; attaching the short connectivity matrix for reference (also in Stephanie's note).

-ben

Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Thanks, team — that guidance is helpful and aligned with our security view. Short answers:

- Atelier's security team will not permit peering in prod (policy: no cross-account route propagation). So PrivateLink is the path we'd prefer for production.
- For PoC we accept short-lived S2S VPN with PSK (security will allow as long as it's timeboxed and monitored).
- I'll have our netops share exact CIDR blocks and the security contact (security@atelier-analytics.com) by EOD tomorrow.

Can you confirm a tentative timeline for PrivateLink ready-for-testing? You mentioned ~3 business days to create the endpoint service — once that's done, what do we need to do on our side to accept and test? Also sending our security whitelist CSV now (security_whitelist.csv).

Appreciate the quick turnaround — looking forward to the PoC.

Best,
Lucas
CTO, Atelier Analytics
